B. Air Pollution
Air pollution resulting from highway construction will be limited. The contractors will be required to use non-burning techniques for the disposal of brush, timber, and other debris. Dust will be kept at a minimum by using moisture treatments to reduce the dust level. Moisture applications, as needed, will also be used during the demolition or removal of the building structures from land acquired for the right-of-way.
C. Water Quality
Oil spillage resulting from vehicles is generally restricted to the riding surface. Because concrete is porous, spillage is normally absorbed within the concrete and the subbase.
In the event of the overturning of a carrier, highway maintenance units would utilize sand and other approved absorbing materials to absorb the spillage. The saturated material would then be disposed of in accordance with the State Environmental Protection Agency "Rules and Regulations".
The present, as well as projected and planned development along Lincoln Highway precludes the necessity of weed or rodent control applications which could possibly contaminate the water sources in the area of the highway.
